page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Running on a KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 40 physical cores operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.8 GB per core. The processor features a 35 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. In CPU-intensive tasks, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1438.99 and a multi-core score of 38378.07, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 34691.95. Memory performance tests show a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 2133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, and a write bandwidth of 48.09 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrated a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 166.28 GB/sec and a static web serving throughput of 25.35 GB/sec. Database operations reached 14249.04 on PassMark, while Redis SET operations achieved 34.78 million operations per second. Large language model inference speeds using a small 135M model reached 1841.39 tokens per second for prompt processing, while a medium 7B model processed prompts at 56.94 tokens per second.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is the complete absence of local storage and GPU hardware, which limits its utility for direct high-speed local disk operations or hardware-accelerated machine learning training. However, the dedicated core allocation and high clock speed of 3.1 GHz provide predictable compute performance. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a balanced resource density for compute-heavy workloads that do not require GPU acceleration or local NVMe drives. It is suitable for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, web serving, database operations, and CPU-based inference tasks.
